oidc.unreachable: The address could not be read from this browser: it may be wrong, or the provider may not let a browser read it. The gateway reads it itself, on the first request.
oidc.notDiscovery: The address answered, but not with an OpenID configuration. It usually ends in /.well-known/openid-configuration.
oidc.noVerification: It offers no way to check a token (introspection_endpoint). Turn on use_jwks under More options to check its signature with the provider's keys instead.
oidc.loginHelp: People in a browser: the gateway sends them to the provider to sign in, then keeps them signed in with a cookie.
oidc.tokenHelp: Applications that already hold a token from the provider: they send it with each request, and the gateway checks it.
oidc.notAbsolute: This is not a full address: a full one starts with https:// (or http://).
oidc.noKeys: It publishes no keys (jwks_uri) to check the tokens it signs.
oidc.redirectHelp: Where the provider sends people back after they sign in: a full address on a path this route matches. Register the same one with the provider.
oidc.redirectMissing: Without it, the gateway sends people back to each page's own address followed by /.apisix/redirect, which changes from page to page: most providers refuse that.
oidc.redirectNotAbsolute: The provider needs a full address here, starting with https:// (or http://), not a path alone.
